title: Optimal Honest Intervals in Multiple Randomization Designs for Two-Sided Marketplaces
banked_reason: All-policy raw-to-grid transfer permits independent actions on disjoint observations, so chi can equal 1 rather than the required n^-3; the load-bearing defect recurred across v2, v3, v4, and v6.
gap_reasons: No rank-K truncated schedule, experiment, likelihood, or calibrated-risk functional is defined.
generic linear contrasts are handled by the displayed formula after Theorem 4.4 and Lemma A.18
The all-policy raw-to-grid discrepancy can equal 1 because policies act independently on the disjoint observation spaces, contradicting the required chi <= n^-3.
proof_attempt_summary: Six proposal revisions developed the exact linear-plus-bilinear MRD decomposition, low-influence Gaussian-chaos approximation, completion-cell finite games, observable interval ideas, and persistent-rank witnesses. The central lower/upper decision transfer collapsed because arbitrary interval policies can act independently on raw and quantized observations, forcing the proposed discrepancy to one; repairing this requires a new exact sufficient-experiment or complete-class theorem, not another local revision.
tldr: Balanced multiple randomization reveals one of four fixed potential outcomes for every buyer--seller pair, leaving the population Neyman scale, cross-world covariance, and interaction alignment latent. The proposal values every interval measurable from the complete observed table. Its finite approximation is a robust game whose first obligation is an exact group-average identity reducing every measurable quantized policy to a row--column orbit rule; each grid row then denotes a cell \(\mathcal B(q)\), while likelihood, coverage, and normalized loss are evaluated for every genuine schedule \(Y\in\mathcal B(q)\). A parameterized cancellation orbit has an unknown direct-effect level that is nevertheless observed exactly and yields strictly shorter expected length than both published analytic competitors, while explicit additive and persistent-rank completion games show that retained spectral directions change finite decision values. The essential target remains the sharp all-observed-policy curve \(R_\alpha(\rho)\), with observable epsilon-attainment and a same-experiment lower bound certified by one finite algorithm.
gap: Published MRD theory supplies unbiased exposure-component variance estimators, a conservative assembled contrast envelope, and Gaussian inference under dominance conditions, but it does not value the best honest interval among all functions of the observed four-block table. Existing completion inversion, expected-measure duality, and slice invariance each omit either global four-schedule compatibility, fixed-half product-slice interactions, or all-rule risk transfer.
fill: An exact policy-symmetrization identity first reduces every measurable randomized quantized rule to the row--column orbit space. Robust completion cells then retain every globally compatible schedule rather than substituting a quantized center, and their common policy is tested against the genuine likelihood, target, and normalization of each cell member; restriction and lifting expose the remaining all-policy discrepancy as \(\chi_{n,K,\eta}\). A parameterized cancellation orbit yields an exact zero-length interval for an unknown direct-effect level and is strictly shorter than both published analytic rules, a persistent-rank subgame proves that the retained spectrum changes a normalized decision value, and the full algorithm must return an observable interval, active-completion dual mixture, value enclosure, and vanishing certificate.
